Former Apple design chief Jony Ive has long described his long-term vision for the iPhone as "a single piece of glass." It is understood that after Ive's departure, Apple has still upheld this goal, and Liquid Glass is the software preparation the company has done for new hardware.

We have already seen numerous reports suggesting that the 20th anniversary edition iPhone may bring us closer to Apple's vision in various ways, and the latest report may add another piece to this puzzle...

Our expectations

Initially some believed Apple might launch a standalone 20th anniversary edition iPhone, but newer reports indicate that all the features designed to achieve the all-glass appearance will be found on the iPhone 19 Pro. To make matters more complicated, some believe that to mark this anniversary, Apple will skip the iPhone 19 naming and go straight to iPhone 20 Pro.

There is still some time before the launch, and these reports are highly speculative, but the most critical design feature is expected to be a display that curves on all four sides, creating the illusion of a completely bezel-less design.

It looks almost certain that this is the year Apple will finally be able to embed the Face ID module under the display, with hopes of also hiding the front camera and speaker beneath the screen.

All of the above designs combined can create a very convincing "single piece of glass" appearance.

Glass back

Leaker Fixed Focus Digital now says this look has another element: the return of a glass back, replacing the aluminium used in recent models.

Although a glass back would make the device more fragile, it does help achieve the "single piece of glass" appearance. Would you consider this trade-off acceptable for a futuristic design? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
